items.claim: Unit display's `accepts` kept through `QuantityView.to`, so typed text reads in the old unit
Typed text with a line break throws a TypeError in `readInfinity`
`percent` speaks a different number than it shows, e.g. 0.145
`spinKey` with an endless max sends ArrowDown from a value above max to Infinity, and the mirror case for min
Fraction counted in a constant reads `1e308π` as Infinity
`multiplier({ symbol: '' })` reads every typed value as NaN
`scientific` shows NaN as `NaN × 10⁰`, with MathML of 10 to the 0
Per-locale caches in `number.ts` and `fieldLocale.ts` have no bound
items.note: (a shared least-recently-used cap of 64 in a new `memo.ts`)

items.claim: `zoom` at 2x or below rounded `z * 100` in binary, so 1.005 showed `100%` where `percent` shows `101%` (sweep, the same mistake as the percent finding)

items.note: a fraction counted in a constant took cubic time on a run of spaces (A); measured 1.5 s at 2,000 spaces and 5 s at 3,000 before the fix
multiplier parse took quadratic time on a run of spaces (A); about 2 s at 60,000 spaces before the fix
a long sum or compound value overflowed the stack in `resolveUnitExpr` (A)
compound unit text took quadratic time in its number of terms (A); 730 ms for 10,000 terms before the fix
`scaleBar` labeled a bar shorter than every unit in the base unit, as `0m` (A)
`QuantityView.to` kept a display naming the old unit, so the result showed `1.2mm` (A)
duplicate of A3 — `resolveUnitExpr` overflowed the stack on a flat chain of terms (B)
duplicate of A2 — multiplier parse was quadratic in a run of spaces (B)
a long digit run ending in junk before a unit took quadratic time (B); 715 ms at 20,000 digits before the fix. Same function as A4, fixed by the same rewrite
fraction and ratio read a division by zero as ±Infinity (B)
a range's dash was spaced for a negative end that shows as `0` (B)
`fraction({ of: 'e' })` took the `e` out of exponent notation, so `1e3` read as 13·e (B)
ordinal spoke a negative with a bare minus sign (B); fixed in `present`'s fallback for every kind with no `speak`, so registered custom kinds are covered too
roman parse did not round a typed decimal (B)

the same infinity-from-digits defect as B4, in other readers: a number whose unit scales it past the range of a number read as Infinity in `unit()`, `bytes()`, `duration()`, and `parseNumber`. Examples are `1e308ft` shown in inches, `1e306TB`, `1e306h`, and a clock duration of 400 digits
`- π`, a sign spaced from the constant, read as NaN in a `fraction({ of: 'π' })` field; it now reads as −π. Fixed by the A1 rewrite and covered by its test

fix: f6440efb3d adds `multiplier()` and `fraction({ of: 'π' })` to the long-text parse property's displays. Before A3's fix that property failed when it happened to draw a long `1e1e…` chain, which was the A3 stack overflow.
